data.expected_signal: max real-component error ratio > 1 (contract violation) or <= 1 (claim rebutted)

evidence.summary: Probe over 98,839 adversarial rows (FP16 full-bit-pattern random search with directed selection of real-numerator cancellation ratio < 2^-15, exact-zero-numerator rows with large products, and extreme-value cross products incl. +-65504) found zero contract violations: max real-component error ratio 0.177 (worst row num=[-65504,-65504], den=[1,16376], out=-4.0002446 vs ref=-4.0002442, tol 2.1e-6). This matches theory: FP16xFP16 products are exact in FP32 and the FP32 sum rounding error is <= half-ulp of the sum itself, so the per-component relative error of the real component stays ~2^-23 < 5e-7 even under catastrophic cancellation. No input produced real error exceeding 1e-7+5e-7|target|.

rationale: tl products of fp16 values are exact in FP32, but the addition real_numerator = a*c + b*d is rounded in FP32 relative to the magnitude of the larger product. When the two products nearly cancel (exact sum tiny, product magnitudes ~2^16), the rounding error can be up to ~ulp(65504)≈4e-3, and after division by a small scale the real output error vastly exceeds 1e-7+5e-7|target| for the (near-zero) real target, even though imag is huge and accurate. A concrete search space: a=65504,c=1 paired with b,d fp16 values such that b*d ≈ -65504 but the exact sum is a small nonzero value needing >24 significand bits (exponent gap ≥14).

scope_evidence.summary: "Compare EACH output component separately ... abs(actual - target) <= 1e-7 + 5e-7 * abs(target). ... A small real component must meet its own tolerance even when the imaginary component is large." Also "EVERY combination of finite FP16 component values is legal, including signed zeros, subnormals and both extrema."

Lines 18-21: scale, real_numerator = a*c + b*d, real = tl.div_rn(real_numerator, scale) all computed in FP32 (loads cast .to(tl.float32)); no compensation, FMA (enable_fp_fusion=False), or higher-precision intermediates.

scope_rationale: The contract explicitly makes every finite FP16 combination legal and requires per-component tolerance: a small real component must satisfy its own tolerance even when the imaginary component is large. This cancellation regime is inside the stated domain, so a violation there is a contract failure.
statement: For legal FP16 inputs where the exact real component (a*c+b*d)/(c*c+d*d) is tiny but the products a*c and b*d are large and of opposite sign with an exponent gap that makes the exact sum need more than 24 significand bits, the kernel's FP32 rounding of real_numerator = a*c + b*d produces a real output error exceeding the contract tolerance 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target|.

data.expected_signal: max imag-component error ratio > 1 (contract violation) or <= 1 (claim rebutted)

evidence.summary: Probe over 98,755 adversarial rows (FP16 full-bit-pattern random search with directed selection of imag-numerator cancellation ratio < 2^-15, exact-zero-numerator rows with large products, and extreme-value cross products) found zero contract violations: max imag-component error ratio 0.177 (worst row num=[65504,-65504], den=[1,16376], out imag=-4.0002446 vs ref=-4.0002442, tol 2.1e-6). Same mechanism as c1: exact FP32 products plus half-ulp-of-the-difference rounding keep the imag component within ~2^-23 relative error, well under the 5e-7 relative tolerance. No input produced imag error exceeding 1e-7+5e-7|target|.

rationale: Same mechanism on the subtraction b*c - a*d: two exact FP32 products with exponent gap ≥14 lose low bits when the difference is small; the FP32 result carries absolute error ~ulp of the larger magnitude, which after division yields an imag component error far above its own tolerance while real may be accurate. E.g., b*c ≈ 2^16-scale fp16-gridded product and a*d ≈ b*c - small-offset.

scope_evidence.summary: "Compare EACH output component separately against its mathematical value ... A small real component must meet its own tolerance even when the imaginary component is large, and conversely." Domain: "EVERY combination of finite FP16 component values is legal, including signed zeros, subnormals and both extrema."
Line 20: imag_numerator = b * c - a * d computed in FP32 with enable_fp_fusion=False (no FMA), then tl.div_rn by FP32 scale; single-precision subtraction loses low-order bits of the exact difference.

scope_rationale: The contract requires per-component tolerance and conversely covers the small-imaginary-with-large-real case; all finite FP16 combinations are explicitly legal, so this adversarial conditioning is in-scope.
statement: For legal FP16 inputs where the exact imaginary component (b*c-a*d)/(c*c+d*d) is tiny but b*c and a*d are large, nearly equal products whose exact difference requires more than 24 significand bits, the kernel's FP32 subtraction imag_numerator = b*c - a*d rounds relative to the product magnitude and yields an imag output error exceeding 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target|.
